plan.title: Feature change
plan.why: Deliver a scoped feature change with a reviewable implementation path.
plan.what:
## Scope

- State the user problem and the intended outcome.
- List what is in and out of scope.

## Commit strategy

- Implement, test, refactor, and document in separate green commits.

milestones.title: Deliver the feature
milestones.desc:
Outcome: As a user, I want the feature, so that the outcome is visible.

Scope: In scope: the reviewed feature and its tests. Out of scope: unrelated changes.

Inputs: The approved definition and the scouted code paths.

Slices: Implement, test, refactor, and document in separate green commits.

tasks.title: Implement the feature
tasks.desc:
Approach: Name the code path, the data shape, and the edge cases the change must handle.

Touch: src/, tests/

Inputs: The approved definition and the scouted touch-points.

Commit: One implementation slice that keeps the tree green.

Verify: The relevant test suite passes.

Guardrails: Keep behavior outside the reviewed scope unchanged.

tasks.title: Test the feature
tasks.desc:
Approach: Cover each acceptance criterion and the edge cases named in the definition.

Touch: tests/

Inputs: The implementation slice and the approved acceptance criteria.

Commit: One test slice that fails without the implementation and passes with it.

Verify: The new tests pass and the relevant suite stays green.

Guardrails: Do not weaken existing assertions to make the new path pass.

tasks.title: Refactor the touched code
tasks.desc:
Approach: Simplify only the area the change touched, without changing behavior.

Touch: src/, tests/

Inputs: A green implementation and its tests.

Commit: One refactor slice with no behavior change.

Verify: The full test suite passes.

Guardrails: Stop when the tests cannot prove the behavior is unchanged.

tasks.title: Update the documentation
tasks.desc:
Approach: Document the new behavior, commands, and limits where users look.

Touch: docs/

Inputs: The final implementation and its verification commands.

Commit: One documentation slice.

Verify: Links and examples resolve against the shipped code.

Guardrails: Do not document planned behavior that the change did not ship.
